Archaic

ar-KAY-ik -- stress on the second syllable, KAY. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Archaic is very old or old-fashioned; belonging to a much earlier time.

The museum displayed archaic farming tools that no modern farmer would recognize, let alone use.

Worked Example

An apprentice blacksmith studies a manual from the 1600s, full of techniques and tools that working smiths abandoned centuries ago.

Methods that belong to a much earlier era -- so old they survive only in manuals and museums -- are archaic. Archaic goes beyond merely old-fashioned: it points to another age entirely.

How Archaic Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

outdated

outdated: no longer current or in general use

antiquated

antiquated: so old-fashioned as to seem unusable

old-fashioned

old-fashioned: belonging to an earlier style or time

Antonyms

modern

modern: of the present time

current

current: in use or happening now

How Strong Is It? — old-fashioned → archaic → antiquated

old-fashioned vs. archaic

old-fashioned vs. archaic: Old-fashioned is gentler than archaic -- an old-fashioned custom belongs to your grandparents' day, while an archaic one belongs to a whole different age, surviving oddly into the present like a fossil.

antiquated vs. archaic

antiquated vs. archaic: Antiquated presses harder than archaic on uselessness: archaic says something comes from a much earlier era, while antiquated adds a shake of the head -- it is so outmoded it barely works in today's world.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of archaic.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — archa-

root — archa-: ancient; beginning (Greek arkhaios 'ancient,' from arkhe 'beginning')

suffix — -ic

suffix — -ic: having the characteristics of; like (Greek -ikos, via Latin -icus)

Put it together

Put it together: Archaic combines Greek arkhaios, 'ancient' -- itself from arkhe, 'beginning', spelled archa- here -- with -ic. Something archaic has the character of the ancient world, of things from the very beginning: language, laws, and tools left over from a much earlier time.

Use the root in a new word: archive

Use the root in a new word: archive: Historians spent the summer in the city archive, reading letters no one had touched for a century.

Root Check

Word Choice

Dictionaries label words 'archaic' when they have dropped out of everyday use -- like 'thee' or 'hither.' Beyond language, archaic fits laws, customs, and technology that belong to a much earlier era; it is stronger and more distant-sounding than plain 'old-fashioned.'
